sourceActivityMap.key: One valid rigid movement is translation (0,+2): y=1 to y=3, A(1,1)->A′(1,3), B(3,1)->B′(3,3). Many maps of the infinite line exist; selected point images must agree with described movement.

From y=1,y=4: translate (0,+2) gives y=3,y=6; half-turn around (0,0) gives y=-1,y=-4; reflect across y=0 gives y=-1,y=-4. All separation 3. For A(1,1), half-turn gives (-1,-1) while reflection gives (1,-1).

Intersect y=0 and y=x at O=(0,0): opposite acute vertical angles both 45°, adjacent obtuse both 135°; a 180° rotation carries each ray to opposite, proving vertical angles equal. Rigid movement cannot send distinct parallel lines to intersecting lines.
y=1 and y=4 translated up 2 become y=3 and y=6, difference 3 preserved. 180° half-turn preserves angle sizes and exchanges opposite rays.
